title: Five weeks of intermittent transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation shape neural networks: a machine learning approach
summary: An SVM classified fALFF network features to distinguish post-transcutaneous-vagus-nerve-stimulation from sham conditions in a controlled study. The result concerns measured imaging changes and does not establish broader therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: An SVM classifies fALFF connectivity features after transcutaneous vagus-nerve stimulation versus sham.
organization: Department of Neurology, University of Lübeck, Lübeck, Germany.

evidence.tested: SVM classification of fALFF network features distinguishes post-tVNS from sham with controlled overfitting, a distinct neural-network finding in a sham-controlled design.
evidence.unknown: Evidence concerns the study’s controlled imaging comparison; durable or clinical therapeutic benefit was not established.
evidence.ai_role: An SVM classifies fALFF connectivity features after transcutaneous vagus-nerve stimulation versus sham.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
